memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's gate 8 (tests/run-all.sh) is not safely wall-clock-predictable: at least one test fixture (the anti-recursion probe used by test-deploy-verify-wiring.sh / test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh) invokes verify-deploy.sh AGAIN from inside gate 8's own run-all.sh pass, and that nested invocation's own run-all.sh is forced to JOBS=1 by the RUN_ALL_NESTED guard. A single top-level `bash verify-deploy.sh .` (no --skip-slow) can therefore take several times longer than its documented ~10 minute solo baseline, with no visible symptom other than gate 8 appearing to hang. Before concluding a full-battery run has hung, check `ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd` for a child verify-deploy.sh process under the top-level one -- if present, this is the known nested-recursion slowdown, not a stuck process or a second battery someone else started.

When extracting an invoked shell-script path from a JSON hook-registration command string with a bash word-split (`read -ra words <<< "$text"`), always strip trailing shell metacharacters (`;`, `)`, `,`, `}`) from the candidate token before testing its file-extension suffix (e.g. `.sh`). A realistic command string can abut a script path directly against punctuation with no intervening whitespace (`bash foo.sh; fi'`), and an extension-suffix test without this strip silently misses such tokens -- discovered via a fixture test case that initially omitted the trailing space the real corpus always happens to have.
